channel.title: Libertas - Freedom Tech Signals
channel.description: Curated insights on freedom technology: Bitcoin, privacy tools, censorship resistance, and digital sovereignty.

item.title: BLM Activist Vanishes from Prison System After Organizing Against Solitary Confinement
item.description: Incarcerated BLM protester Malik Muhammad disappeared from tracking systems before surfacing 3,000 miles away in South Carolina, allegedly in retaliation for organizing a class-action lawsuit against Oregon's solitary confinement practices.

item.title: Hungary Drops Charges Against Pride Organizers Following EU Court Ruling
item.description: Hungarian prosecutors dropped charges against Pride event organizers after European Court of Justice ruled Hungary's 2021 anti-LGBT law incompatible with EU law, signaling restoration of rule of law.

item.title: EFF Demands Warrant Requirement for Section 702 Surveillance or Full Expiration
item.description: EFF is taking a hardline stance on Section 702 renewal: either require warrants for FBI queries of Americans' communications or let the mass surveillance authority expire entirely.

item.title: US Treasury Sanctions Iran's Largest Crypto Exchange Nobitex
item.description: US Treasury sanctioned Nobitex, which handled over half of Iran's crypto inflows in 2023, as part of broader crackdown on Iranian cryptocurrency infrastructure.

item.title: California Expands Age-Gating to Browsers/Websites, Exempts Open Source
item.description: CA's AB 1856 exempts open-source OS from age verification while expanding mandatory age-bracketing from OS/app stores to all browsers and websites.

item.title: Treasury Nominee Bessent Reiterates Opposition to CBDC, Pushes Crypto Clarity Act
item.description: Treasury Secretary nominee Scott Bessent reaffirmed opposition to a U.S. central bank digital currency and urged Congress to pass cryptocurrency regulatory clarity legislation.

item.title: Russia Bans 9 LGBT Rights Groups as 'Extremist,' Creating Demand for Secure Comms
item.description: Russian courts banned 9 LGBT support organizations as 'extremist' with up to 12-year prison penalties, forcing groups to seek censorship-resistant tools to continue operations.

item.title: Researchers Document 'Chilling Effect' of Government Surveillance on Free Speech
item.description: Citizen Lab researchers argue that surveillance and government threats are causing widespread self-censorship among Americans, creating a chilling effect that extends far beyond campus protests.

item.title: NSO Group Caught Violating Court Order by Targeting WhatsApp Users
item.description: WhatsApp detected NSO Group conducting phishing attacks against its users despite existing court orders prohibiting such activities, highlighting continued state-level surveillance threats.

item.title: EFF Warns Congress: AI-Powered Government Surveillance Threatens Constitutional Rights
item.description: EFF testified to Congress that government adoption of AI for mass surveillance would supercharge unconstitutional civil liberties violations, calling for strong safeguards before deployment.

item.title: Rwanda Arrests YouTube Journalists for Exposing Secret Detention Facility
item.description: Two journalists from YouTube channel Imbarutso ya Demokarasi were arrested and charged for reporting on Kwa Kabuga, an unofficial detention center in Kigali where authorities hold 'undesirable' people.

item.title: White House Frames Crypto Clarity Act as 'Pro-Enforcement' Bill
item.description: White House crypto adviser Patrick Witt defends the Clarity Act as a 'pro-enforcement bill' despite industry pushback, as lawmakers rush to pass the legislation.

item.title: Speculative 2036 Bitcoin Vision: Global Settlement Layer for Stablecoins and AI Commerce
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine piece envisions 2036 scenario where Bitcoin serves as invisible settlement infrastructure for stablecoins and AI agent transactions, with self-custody becoming default through better wallet design.

item.title: California's A.B. 412 Would Create Impossible AI Compliance Burden, Crush Open Source
item.description: California's A.B. 412 demands AI developers identify all copyrighted training data, but EFF warns this is technically impossible and would lock in Big Tech monopolies while crushing small developers and open-source projects.

item.title: JPMorgan CEO Dimon Declares War on Crypto Clarity Act, Attacks Coinbase
item.description: JPMorgan's Jamie Dimon vows to fight the Clarity Act, claiming it lets crypto firms operate like banks without regulatory obligations, while calling Coinbase CEO Armstrong 'full of sh*t'.

item.title: Circle Freezes $12.6M USDC Linked to Privacy Protocol Zama
item.description: Circle froze $12.6M USDC connected to privacy protocol Zama, reportedly due to unrelated civil court case, highlighting centralized stablecoin control risks.

item.title: Schneier: Systematic Chilling Effects as Government Strategy Against Dissent
item.description: Bruce Schneier and Jon Penney analyze how surveillance, threats, and abuse of power create systematic chilling effects that suppress dissent and activism, arguing this represents a deliberate strategy rather than incidental government overreach.

item.title: LONDA 2025 Report: Africa's Digital Rights Show Mixed Progress Amid Authoritarian Pushback
item.description: Paradigm Initiative's LONDA 2025 report reveals stark digital rights divide across 29 African countries, with some nations enacting progressive privacy laws while others intensify internet shutdowns, surveillance, and activist arrests.

item.title: BLM Activist Vanishes in Prison System After Cross-Country Transfer
item.description: Incarcerated activist Malik Muhammad disappeared from tracking systems for weeks before surfacing 3,000 miles away in South Carolina, allegedly as retaliation for prison organizing efforts.

item.title: EFF Names Nicole Ozer as New Executive Director
item.description: Electronic Frontier Foundation announces Nicole Ozer as new Executive Director, bringing two decades of privacy legislation and surveillance oversight experience including authoring California's warrant requirement for electronic data access.

item.title: Senate Dems Block NSA Surveillance Renewal Over Trump Intel Chief Pick
item.description: Senate Democrats united to block renewal of NSA's Section 702 surveillance program after Trump appointed Bill Pulte, who allegedly misused government databases for political vendettas, as intel chief.

item.title: Bangladesh: Police Profile Journalists as Persecution Cycle Continues Under New Government
item.description: CPJ reports Bangladesh's new PM Tarique Rahman continues cycle of journalist persecution after 100 days in office, with police conducting background checks and profiling journalists nationwide.

item.title: Texas Forms Bitcoin Reserve Committee, Moves to Direct BTC Custody
item.description: Texas announced a 5-member advisory committee for its Strategic Bitcoin Reserve and issued RFP for crypto custodian to transition from ETF exposure to direct Bitcoin custody.

item.title: Azerbaijan Seeks 16-Year Prison Terms for Independent Media Workers Over Foreign Funding
item.description: Azerbaijani prosecutors seek up to 16 years in prison for 9 journalists and media workers from Toplum TV and affiliated organizations, charged with using Western donor funds in violation of local laws.

item.title: Russia Labels OVD-Info Rights Group 'Extremist' for Helping Protesters
item.description: Russia designated OVD-Info, a prominent rights group that provides legal aid to protesters and documents police abuses, as 'extremist' alongside 35 other organizations on June 4, 2026.

item.title: Tails 7.8.1 Emergency Release Fixes Critical Privilege Escalation Vulnerability
item.description: Tails released emergency update fixing serious Linux kernel vulnerability (CVE-2026-43503) that could allow privilege escalation and complete system compromise, plus Tor client security fixes.

item.title: Citizen Lab Exposes Mobile Networks as Covert Surveillance Platforms
item.description: New Citizen Lab research reveals how weaknesses in mobile network technology and governance enable sophisticated surveillance campaigns targeting users.

item.title: EFF Challenges State Social Media Bans for Youth Based on 'Shockingly Shaky Science'
item.description: Electronic Frontier Foundation argues that multiple states rushing to ban youth social media access are relying on flawed research and 'pop psychology' rather than settled science, threatening constitutional rights.

item.title: Fusion Centers Monitor Social Media for AI Data Center Critics, Labeling Speech as Terror Risk
item.description: Philadelphia fusion center surveillance bulletin obtained by The Intercept shows police monitoring social media posts critical of AI data centers, classifying "disruptive First Amendment activity" as domestic terrorism indicators.

item.title: EFF Warns Age Verification Creates Mass Surveillance Infrastructure
item.description: EFF highlights how age verification mandates force users to submit sensitive personal data to third parties, creating centralized honeypots that have already been breached multiple times.

item.title: US Congress Moves to Permanently Integrate Israeli AI Surveillance Tech Into Military
item.description: House defense bill includes Section 224 creating permanent framework to integrate Israeli AI, autonomous systems, and surveillance tech into US military operations, raising concerns about domestic surveillance capabilities.

item.title: Meta Accuses NSO of Violating Court Injunction with New WhatsApp Attacks
item.description: Meta claims NSO Group violated a permanent injunction by conducting new spear phishing attacks on WhatsApp users, seeking contempt charges against the blacklisted spyware company.

item.title: Pentagon Uses AI-Generated Content Mill to Spread Propaganda in Latin America
item.description: Investigation reveals U.S. military operates La Tilde, an AI-powered propaganda site targeting Latin American audiences with pro-Pentagon content disguised as independent journalism.

item.title: Bangladesh Deploys AI Traffic Cameras for Automated Surveillance and Case Filing in Dhaka
item.description: Bangladesh launched AI-powered traffic cameras in Dhaka that automatically scan license plates, file cases, and send prosecution notices without human involvement—marking the country's first fully automated digital enforcement system.

item.title: Mali Arrests Journalists Under Cybercrime Law for Factual Reporting
item.description: Mali's military junta arrested two journalists under cybercrime laws for stating basic facts - one for criticizing misuse of cyber legislation, another for reporting territorial control by armed groups.

item.title: US Fusion Centers Surveilling AI Critics on Social Media
item.description: Philadelphia fusion center is monitoring Americans' social media posts critical of AI data centers, labeling routine First Amendment activity as potential domestic violent extremism.

item.title: Meta Smart Glasses Hide Unreleased Face Recognition System
item.description: Code review reveals Meta embedded unreleased face-recognition system in smart glasses that identifies people using biometric data stored on users' phones.

item.title: Iranian-American Journalist Reports Torture from Evin Prison in Smuggled Recording
item.description: Jailed Iranian-American journalist Reza Valizadeh smuggled out voice memo from Evin Prison detailing physical torture, psychological abuse, and medical neglect, highlighting risks faced by press freedom advocates.

item.title: Bangladesh's Cycle of Press Repression Continues Under New Government
item.description: After 100 days in office, PM Tarique Rahman's government continues systematic persecution of journalists through detention, surveillance, and repressive cyber laws despite election pledges to protect press freedom.

item.title: China Pressures Zambia to Cancel Major Digital Rights Conference RightsCon
item.description: Chinese government pressure forced cancellation of RightsCon 2026 in Zambia after officials objected to planned discussions of China's digital authoritarianism and Taiwanese activist participation.

item.title: Kazakhstan Forces Anti-War Orthodox Priest Into Psychiatric Detention
item.description: Kazakhstan authorities transferred activist priest Yakov Vorontsov to psychiatric facility on dubious drug charges, following years of pressure over his anti-war stance and efforts to establish independent Orthodox community.

item.title: US Treasury Seizes Nearly $1B in Iranian Crypto Assets
item.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent disclosed the U.S. has seized nearly $1 billion in cryptocurrency assets from Iran, demonstrating state capacity for large-scale crypto confiscation.

item.title: EFF Warns Congress About AI-Powered Mass Government Surveillance Risks
item.description: EFF testified to Congress that government adoption of AI for mass surveillance would supercharge unconstitutional civil liberties violations, citing AI errors and lack of transparency.

item.title: NY Court Case Challenges State Claims to 'Lost' Bitcoin Wallets
item.description: New York lawsuit seeks ownership of nearly 40,000 Bitcoin wallets; amicus brief argues state lost-and-found laws can't claim assets controlled by private keys.

item.title: Anthropic Takes Funding from UAE Surveillance State While Condemning AI Authoritarianism
item.description: Anthropic raised $95B from UAE's MGX fund while publishing anti-authoritarian AI policy, exposing double standards as UAE uses AI for surveillance and repression.

item.title: Court Order Freezes $12.6M in Zama's Confidential USDC Contract
item.description: Circle froze $12.6M in Zama's confidential USDC contract following a court order related to Overnight Finance lawsuit, highlighting vulnerability of privacy tech to state intervention.

item.title: EFF Defends Anti-Surveillance Site Against Flock Safety Legal Threats
item.description: EFF successfully defended DeFlock.me, a grassroots website tracking ALPR surveillance cameras, against cease-and-desist threats from police tech company Flock Safety.

item.title: Zimbabwe Opposition Activist Freed After 7 Months Detention, Torture
item.description: Zimbabwe court acquitted opposition activist Godfrey Karembera after 7 months detention on protest charges, following abduction, torture, and repeated bail denials by authorities.

item.title: China Intensifies Tiananmen Censorship with Advanced Algorithmic Filtering
item.description: Chinese authorities are deploying sophisticated censorship algorithms that can flag indirect references like 'one banana and four apples' as Tiananmen symbols, while expanding surveillance to license plates and social gatherings.

item.title: EFF Exposes ALPR Mission Creep: License Plate Cameras Now Track Noise Complaints
item.description: EFF reports widespread surveillance expansion as automated license plate readers, originally for safety, now track citizens for minor infractions like noise complaints.

item.title: Meta Removes Facial Recognition from Smart Glasses After EFF Exposes Surveillance Code
item.description: Meta quietly removed facial recognition code from its smart glasses app after EFF and WIRED exposed the surveillance capability that could identify strangers in public.

item.title: 200+ Crypto Companies Push Senate to Vote on Digital Asset Clarity Act
item.description: Coalition of 200+ companies including Coinbase, Circle, and a16z urge Senate leaders to bring the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act to floor vote, seeking regulatory framework to define SEC vs CFTC jurisdiction over digital assets.

item.title: Microsoft Threatens Legal Action Against Researcher Who Broke BitLocker
item.description: Anonymous security researcher 'Nightmare Eclipse' published exploits breaking Microsoft BitLocker encryption, prompting Microsoft to threaten legal action against the disclosure.

item.title: Global Age Verification Mandates Create Massive Surveillance Infrastructure
item.description: Governments worldwide are implementing age verification systems requiring identity checks to access online platforms, creating unprecedented surveillance infrastructure that threatens privacy and anonymity for all users.

item.title: House Rushes Through Copyright Office Overhaul That Threatens Digital Rights
item.description: House passed H.R. 6028 restructuring the Copyright Office, making it more political and concentrating power in a presidential appointee, threatening fair use and circumvention rights.

item.title: Bitcoin Book Excerpt Illustrates Inflation's Impact on Purchasing Power Over 40 Years
item.description: New book excerpt uses German ice cream prices to demonstrate how inflation destroyed 80% of purchasing power over 40 years, positioning Bitcoin's fixed supply as alternative.

item.title: Scientists Ejected from Diabetes Conference for Distributing Critical Editorial
item.description: Five prominent diabetes researchers were physically removed from the American Diabetes Association conference for distributing copies of a published editorial criticizing Trump administration attacks on scientific research.

item.title: Russian Journalist Detained for Telegram Comments, Faces 7 Years in Prison
item.description: Russian authorities detained journalist Aleksey Seregin for 'justifying terrorism' over a 2024 Telegram comment about Chechen independence, highlighting risks of using mainstream platforms under authoritarian regimes.

item.title: US Health Aid Tied to Surveillance Access and Pathogen Data Extraction
item.description: Human Rights Watch reveals US bilateral health agreements condition aid on broad surveillance access to health data and extractive rights to pathogen samples, raising major privacy and sovereignty concerns.

item.title: Meta Deploys Hidden Facial Recognition in Always-On Smart Glasses
item.description: Meta has secretly deployed facial recognition code to millions of Ray-Ban smart glasses, creating a distributed surveillance network that converts faces into biometric faceprints for identification.

item.title: UK's New Crime and Policing Act 2026 Introduces 'Cumulative Disruption' Protest Restrictions
item.description: UK's Crime and Policing Act 2026 allows police to restrict protests based on 'cumulative disruption' from unrelated previous protests, threatening sustained activism and civil society accountability mechanisms.

item.title: Citizen Lab Director Details Greek Predator Spyware Scandal Investigation
item.description: Citizen Lab's Ron Deibert spoke about exposing Intellexa's Predator spyware use against Greek journalists and politicians, triggering national and EU investigations.

item.title: Access Now Report: Data Privacy as Defense Against Electoral Disinformation in Latin America
item.description: Access Now analysis shows how mass data collection enables personalized disinformation campaigns and proposes privacy law enforcement as key defense for upcoming Latin American elections.

item.title: Russian Ruble Stablecoin Processes $110B Despite Western Sanctions
item.description: Russian ruble-backed stablecoin A7A5 has processed over $110 billion in transactions, demonstrating effective circumvention of Western financial sanctions through cryptocurrency infrastructure.

item.title: Jordan Uses Cybercrime Law to Prosecute Facebook Posts Criticizing Israel Relations
item.description: Jordanian activist Ayman Sandouka sentenced to 5 years for peaceful Facebook post criticizing King's Israel policy, highlighting systematic use of 2023 cybercrime law to suppress online dissent.

item.title: EFF Warns Congress Against AI-Powered Mass Government Surveillance
item.description: EFF testified to Congress that government adoption of AI without strong safeguards would supercharge unconstitutional mass surveillance and civil liberties violations.

item.title: NASA Satellites Can Detect GPS Jammers from Space, Raising Privacy Concerns
item.description: NASA satellites originally designed for weather monitoring can now locate GPS jammers within several kilometers, potentially enabling state surveillance of privacy tools used by activists and dissidents.

item.title: Ethiopia Election: Systematic Press Censorship and Phone Searches Target Journalists
item.description: Ethiopian authorities are detaining journalists, searching their phones, and revoking media licenses ahead of June elections, creating what reporters call a climate of fear that has crippled independent election coverage.

item.title: Trump Appoints Unqualified Acting DNI as Section 702 Surveillance Powers Face Renewal
item.description: Trump appointed Bill Pulte, who lacks intelligence experience but has weaponized government data against political foes, as acting DNI as Congress debates renewing Section 702 warrantless surveillance powers.

item.title: EFF Launches Enshittification Merch to Fund Digital Rights Work
item.description: EFF releases merchandise featuring Cory Doctorow's 'enshittification' emoji under Creative Commons license, with proceeds funding digital rights advocacy against surveillance capitalism and tech monopolies.
